text:
ravi: Heads-up: a partner integration returned a model response that passed our model-level checks but failed the structured-output gate. It was routed to fallback and customer complained about being billed.

anna: Quick sample?

ravi: payload we logged (redacted): `{"operation":"create","params":["team-9","Bug"]}`  params is an array; our schema expects `params` as an object `{team_id, title}`.

jia: Router currently treats schema mismatches as enforce (hard) by default. That triggers degen routing.

ops-bot: :rotating_light: validation.rejected spike on cluster-b (2m window)

miguel: Two problems: visibility for support + fairness for billing. Suggest we: 1) add `validation_reason` to traces, 2) expose a redacted, human-friendly hint in Console behind a per-org opt-in, 3) add a non-blocking `validate=observe` mode for 0.5% sampling to measure impact.

anna: I'm wary of auto-coercion. If we add adapter coercion it must be reversible and conservative (positional->named only when mapping is explicit). Enterprise customers should opt-in.

ravi: Agreed. Proposal: header `x-validate-mode: observe|soft|strict`. Observe = record only, soft = attempt coercion then flag but keep original routing, strict = enforce and fallback on mismatch. Default: strict for public API but observe for new connectors rollout.

jia: Implementation notes: emit metrics `validation.mismatch_total{route,model}` and `validation.coercion_applied_total`. Also add span tag `validator.hint` for UI consumption.

miguel: Billing doc change: clarify we bill for attempted model runs; support can offer pro-rated credits when validation clearly misapplied. Samir/finance should review.

ravi: Action items: jia to add metrics + span tags, anna to draft adapter coercion lib with reversible ops, miguel to write Console mock with opt-in toggle + privacy text, ops-bot to create alert if mismatch rate > 3/min for 10m. Sync in 25m.
